title: app landing: a nav entry whose dataSource read is pending is skipped as the landing (and an all-bound app flashes no-access)
body:
## Problem

objectui#13029 (PR #13095) makes a navigation entry's declared API `dataSource` feed its `visible`, failing closed: an entry whose read is pending or failed is hidden. That is the card's rule, and the sidebar, `nav:menu` and the command palette honour it.

`AppRootLanding` (`packages/app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx`) chooses an app's landing from `navEntriesShownToMember(…, gates)`. A pending entry is dropped there, and `appServesNoNavigation` is then asked over the filtered trees. The contract review of PR #13095 (on objectui#13029) reads two consequences that are new with that PR, because bound entries used to be ignored and therefore shown:

1. **An app whose entries are all bound** shows `AppNoAccessEmptyState` until the reads answer, then re-renders and navigates. The user sees a "no access" flash.
2. **An app whose first entry is bound and whose second is plain** navigates (with `replace`) to the second entry on first render, before the read answers. A pending bound entry can never be the landing, even when its read would have shown it.

Both are source readings from the review. Neither has been measured in a browser.

## Target

The landing waits on, or re-resolves after, the reads of the entries it would choose between. Pick one of these and pin it:
- (A) While any entry ahead of the first plain one is pending, the landing holds (the splash or a skeleton, not the no-access state), then lands on the first entry the member is shown once the reads have answered.
- (B) A ruling that first-render landing on the first plain entry is intended. Then only (1)'s no-access flash is fixed: hold while every candidate is pending.

objectui#12426's rule ("the landing is the first entry this member is shown") reads closer to (A).

## Acceptance

- Pins through the real `AppRootLanding`:
  - all-bound pending shows no `AppNoAccessEmptyState`;
  - first-bound pending, then `ready` and shown, lands on the bound entry (A) or on the plain one (B), as ruled;
  - a failed read lands on the next shown entry;
  - an app with no bound entry lands on first render exactly as today (control).
- One measured browser reading of an app whose first nav entry is bound (cloud#3002's 环境 row is the named consumer).

## Surface

`packages/app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx` (`AppRootLanding`), `utils/appServesNoNavigation.ts` if the predicate needs a pending state, `hooks/useNavMemberGates.ts` (it already exposes the read state), and tests beside them.

Filed from the objectui#13029 contract review (PR #13095) by `domain:ui` seat 2 (`session_01XVp19E1MYUTFM3dnkwz8gB`).
